# View — catch up without changing the work

Resolve the selected home, project and mapped code using
`references/workspace-records.md`. Read the original tasks, relevant ideas and
retained docs and linked decisions/evidence, including unmigrated legacy thoughts.
Docs supply applicable knowledge and constraints, not new tasks or cleanup candidates.
Check fresh Git HEAD, working changes and actual
verification instead of repeating a stale next-action note.

Lead with the current result, next action and decisions that need the user. Keep
planned, implemented, verified, blocked and awaiting-owner work distinct. Show
concurrent open work and the user's current priorities. Ideas remain possible
work; the queue is not execution authorization. A passing build or engineering
check does not satisfy an outstanding human acceptance gate.

Read only. Do not correct records, change dates or priorities, create tasks, run
implementation or migrate the workspace. If records disagree with code, report the
discrepancy and evidence rather than silently repairing them. Report unavailable
repositories and unknown provenance; never substitute the home repository's HEAD.
Use shape-add for a requested record update and shape-next for authorized
continuation, without requiring a literal skill-tool call or a view-first sequence.

Use the optional `scripts/workspace --root <home> status <project>` reader when it
helps. Report standard records, readable non-standard records or absent records.
Read `references/session-handoff.md` and `references/legacy-blueprints.md` when
legacy boards or handoffs carry unique context; preserve them in place.

A normal status reply stays in chat. An explicitly requested graph may use a
fresh `view` output in session scratch, served at a clickable URL. That disposable
snapshot does not own state and does not authorize a persistent index or report.
